planting.note: Divide back bulbs with at least two to three growths attached right after flowering finishes; give a bright spot and a cool autumn night drop to trigger the next season's spikes.

directions: First exhibited in 1922, this individual clone of the Cymbidium Alexanderi grex turned out to carry four sets of chromosomes instead of the usual two, a spontaneous tetraploid mutation that gave it unusually thick substance, broader petals, and far greater vigor than its diploid grex-mates. Breeders quickly recognized its potential and used it heavily through the mid-20th century, so a large share of the sturdy, large-flowered cymbidium hybrids sold today carry 'Westonbirt' somewhere in their ancestry. Flowers are broad, waxy, and pale cream to white with rose-red lip markings, held in gracefully arching sprays over winter. Keep it in a large, barely root-bound pot of coarse bark, water freely through active growth, and provide a distinct autumn temperature drop to reliably initiate spikes.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society International Orchid Register
